chunks: Al-Husayn b. Ahmad b. Idris (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to me from Ayyub b. Nuh from Muhammad b. Ziyad from Ghiyath b. Ibrahim from al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad from his father from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said:

The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) said: Whoever does good in what remains of his life will not be taken to account for what has passed of his sins. And whoever does evil in what remains of his life will be taken to account for both the first and the last.

key_terms.أحسن: to do good, to act virtuously
key_terms.أساء: to do evil, to act wrongly
key_terms.يؤاخذ: to be held accountable, to be taken to task

ai.seo_question: What does Islam teach about repentance and good deeds erasing past sins?
ai.summary: This prophetic tradition, narrated through Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) from his forefathers, conveys a powerful message of hope and warning from the Prophet Muhammad (S). It teaches that sincere repentance and good deeds in the remainder of one's life can erase past sins, but continued wrongdoing compounds both past and present transgressions. This hadith was likely shared to encourage believers to seize the opportunity of repentance regardless of their past.
word_analysis: may Allah have mercy on him

en.bilal-muhammad: Al-Husayn b. Ahmad b. Idris (rh) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to me from Ayyub b. Nuh from Muhammad b. Ziyad from Ghiyath b. Ibrahim from al-Sadiq Ja`far b. Muhammad from his father from his forefathers (as). He said:

The Messenger of Allah (s) said: Whoever does good for the remainder of his life will not be taken for his past sins. Whoever does evil for the remainder of his life will be taken for his past and his end.
